name: Iskander-M
note: Road-mobile SRBM system (9K720, NATO SS-26 'Stone'). The 9P78 TEL carries two 9M723 ballistic missiles and can also fire 9M728/9M729 ground-launched cruise missiles. Depressed, manoeuvring (up to 30 g) trajectory; 10-50 m CEP with the optical seeker. Figures are for the Russian 9M723 (Iskander-M); the export 9M720 is limited to 280 km.

source.title: 9K720 Iskander (SS-26) | Missile Threat (CSIS)
source.note: 9M723 maximum range 500 km (quoted 400-500 km), payload 480-700 kg. The export 9M720 is reduced to 280 km.

source.title: 9K720 Iskander (SS-26) | Missile Threat (CSIS)
source.note: Each 9P78 TEL carries two missiles; a brigade fields 12 TELs (reportedly moving to 16).

name: ATACMS
note: MGM-140 Army Tactical Missile System, a road-mobile SRBM fired from the M270 MLRS (2 rounds) or M142 HIMARS (1 round). Figures are for the in-service Block 1A / unitary (300 km); the older Block 1 reached only 165 km. Being replaced by the PrSM (Precision Strike Missile).

source.title: MGM-140 Army Tactical Missile System (ATACMS) | Missile Threat (CSIS)
source.note: Block 1A maximum range 300 km with the submunition warhead (270 km unitary). Block 1 was 165 km.

source.title: MGM-140 Army Tactical Missile System (ATACMS) | Missile Threat (CSIS)
source.note: 'The Block 1A has a minimum range of 100 km.'

source.title: MGM-140 Army Tactical Missile System (ATACMS) | Missile Threat (CSIS)
source.note: An M270 MLRS carries two ATACMS (in place of 12 rockets); a HIMARS carries one.

name: DF-21D
note: Anti-ship variant of the DF-21 (CSS-5) MRBM, the 'carrier-killer'. Road-mobile TEL. Uses a manoeuvring reentry vehicle with a terminal seeker to hit moving ships; ~20 m CEP. The land-attack DF-21C and nuclear DF-21A share the airframe (base DF-21 reaches ~2,150 km).

source.title: DF-21 (CSS-5) | Missile Threat (CSIS)
source.note: 'U.S. reports suggest a range of 1,450 to 1,550 km' for the DF-21D anti-ship variant; ~20 m CEP maneuverable warhead. This is a US estimate; the land-attack DF-21C reaches ~2,150 km.

name: DF-26
note: Road-mobile IRBM ('Guam killer'), China's first conventional ballistic missile able to strike Guam. Hot-swappable nuclear or conventional warhead; the DF-26B anti-ship variant carries a terminal seeker for moving ships. ~150-450 m CEP. A brigade fields 12-18 TELs.

source.title: DF-26 | Missile Threat (CSIS)
source.note: Two-stage solid IRBM, range 4,000 km (NASIC), payload 1,200-1,800 kg. The DF-26B anti-ship variant engages moving ships at intermediate range.

name: Typhon / Tomahawk (land)
note: Land-based Typhon (Mid-Range Capability) ground launcher firing the Tomahawk Block IV/V subsonic cruise missile (the same launcher also fires the SM-6). Figures are for the Block IV TLAM-E land-attack Tomahawk; the Maritime Strike Tomahawk (Block Va) adds an anti-ship seeker. The retired nuclear TLAM-N reached 2,500 km.

source.title: Tomahawk | Missile Threat (CSIS)
source.note: 'The Block IV TLAM-E has a range of 900 nautical miles or 1,600 km'; subsonic, low-altitude, <10 m CEP, 1,000 lb unitary warhead. Anti-ship reach is restored by the Maritime Strike Tomahawk.

name: K-300P Bastion-P
note: Mobile coastal-defence system (NATO SS-C-5 'Stooge') firing the P-800 Oniks/Yakhont (SS-N-26) supersonic (Mach 2.5) anti-ship / land-attack cruise missile. A battery has four launcher vehicles of two missiles each. Sea-skimming terminal phase; fire-and-forget active/passive radar seeker.

source.title: K-300P Bastion-P 'SS-C-5 Stooge' | Weapons Parade
source.note: 'Maximum range about 450 km against land targets, 350 km against naval targets'; Mach 2.5. A low-low sea-skimming profile shortens this to roughly 120-300 km.

source.title: K-300P Bastion-P 'SS-C-5 Stooge' | Weapons Parade
source.note: '4 launchers with 2 missiles each' per battery.

name: BrahMos (land)
note: Ground-launched BrahMos (PJ-10), an Indo-Russian supersonic (Mach 2.0-2.8) anti-ship / land-attack cruise missile derived from the P-800 Oniks. Ramp or vertical launcher. Baseline range 290-450 km; extended-range variants reach further. The export version is capped at 290 km under the MTCR.

source.title: BrahMos | Missile Threat (CSIS)
source.note: 'Range of between 300-500 km depending on which variant and launch platform is used'; export capped at 290 km (MTCR). 400 km taken as a mid figure for the current land variant; extended-range versions go further.
